prs.title: Classify equal-weight cubic repairs by a Pell recurrence (no κ)
prs.summary:
## Change and mathematical scope

This answers **Open next question 2 of Nick Petalas's #6653**: do its equal-weight cubic repairs at arities 7 and 97 extend to an infinite family?

For every integer `r>2`, the fixed defect representation

```text
sum_{i<r}(A+iB)^3 - r*A^3
  = -r*A^3 + (r/2)*(A+dB)^3 + (r/2)*(A+eB)^3
```

holds with rational directions exactly when `r^2-3*n^2=1` for a positive integer `n`, with `{d,e}={(r-1-n)/2,(r-1+n)/2}`. The directions are automatically integers. An elementary descent proves that the recurrence `(r,n)->(2r+3n,r+2n)` from `(1,0)` exhausts the solutions.

An infinite subsequence lies outside all earlier infinite classes listed by #6653: `7,97,18817,262087,50843527,...`. The first two remain Petalas's finite examples. Visiting directions `e,d,0` gives **three queries and three integer shears**, restores arbitrary dirty sources, retains every original child and produces the eager output. With #6212's cited dyadic lower bound, the query minimum is exactly three at these arities. No shear-optimality claim.

**Scoped written proof with exact checks; no new κ or supplier admission.** This classifies the fixed weights, not arbitrary three-query repairs.

prs.title: Prove exact common-pairing capacity under coordinate uncertainty (no κ)
prs.summary:
## Summary

Scoped written algebraic proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. For any field, nominal matrix B and independently uncertain coordinate set E, the exact common identity-pairing capacity is

```text
max { r : X (B + sum_E t_ij E_ij) Y = I_r for every t }
  = max { rank B[A,C] : (A times C) intersect E is empty }.
```

X and Y may be dense but must be fixed across alternatives. A nonsingular clean minor supplies attaining maps. The nominal map plus each single-entry alternative already forces the full bound.

For B=I, the exact capacity is the independence number of the error-support graph, with loops forbidden. A directed n-cycle has capacity floor(n/2), even though every nominal/single-entry map is invertible. The five-cycle therefore has exactly two common channels despite each map individually having rank five. Correlated-error and nonidentity-nominal witnesses delimit the theorem.

prs.title: Sharpen compiler width divisors with exact plateau visit counts (no κ)
prs.summary:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration: sharpen the plateau-product divisor for the separated chronological compiler of CubeJerry's [#7424](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7424). This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

```text
old exponent on every plateau: tau = A*ceil(log2 k_min)
new exact maximum visits:     nu = 1+floor((min(N,A*gamma_next-1)-A*gamma)/delta)
uniform consequence:          nu <= A-1 < tau

B_n divides product_gamma S(gamma)^nu_gamma, for every n <= N.
```

Here delta is the smallest positive fresh-source rank on the plateau. Paid exits always leave that plateau; each complement step inside it subtracts at least delta. Applying the exact visit count to every prime-valuation chain proves the smaller divisor. The new divisor divides the old one, strictly whenever an observed plateau has source count greater than one.

For A=64, N=127, targets (2,3) and one paid rank-1 site, the upper divisor decreases from 2^64 to the attained 2^32. The width formula is credited prior work in #7424; the new result is the general bound. No new kappa or changed width sequence is claimed.

prs.title: Prove endpoint sign criterion for fully crossing helper bills (no κ)
prs.summary:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR #7331 leaves open whether a proper-terminal helper rank bill can be positive inside a feasible interval while both endpoint bills are nonpositive. This proves **no, for every finite number of unit-charged paths reaching the terminal**.

For `0<t<1`, `0<=a_i<=T<=b_i`, `A=max a_i`, and
`G(x)=x^t+(T-x)^t-T^t-sum_i[(x-a_i)^t+(b_i-x)^t-(b_i-a_i)^t]`:

```text
There exists x in [A,T] with G(x)>0  iff  G(A)>0.
```

A self-contained elementary proof shows that each path's split cost divided by the helper's split benefit is nondecreasing. Thus the normalized bill is nonincreasing. The result handles real endpoints, A=0, A=T and every permitted closed subinterval. It preserves #7331's negative interior-maximum counterexample: it decides positivity, not the maximizing dimension. A new exact positive fractional-weight counterexample prevents broadening the zero-endpoint criterion to arbitrary charges.

**No new κ, supplier admission, emitted word or selected-frontier change.** Paths ending before T, actual cut legality, ordinary charges, native realization, ownership and restoration remain separate.
